text: Registered 2026-11-11 as an unsealed proposal under the system-table-retention epic (owner request that day, during the formation-stability takeover). Size L. No seal, receipt or measurement is created by this entry. Two holds before sealing: (1) the epic deletion gate, three consecutive lab passes of the fresh-formation scenario and CDC delivery stages 1-3 landed; (2) the open owner ruling, what a deterministic-intent retry answers when its earlier terminal row has been retired (today a missing row makes the retry a silent fresh execution). Next owner for (2): the repository owner. The dependency list is the 2026-11-11 census list; re-verify it against current source at seal, since a dependency added after the census is not in it.

Open owner ruling (asked 2026-11-11): what a deterministic-intent retry answers once its earlier terminal row has been retired. Alternatives put to the owner: (1) never retire a row a retry could still reach (horizon longer than any retry lifetime plus a reference check) — no semantic change, but needs a provable retry-lifetime bound and schema jobs can stay pending indefinitely; (2) compact 'retired intent' marker (id, outcome, time) — keeps exactly-once answers at ~100 B, but is still unbounded and a second representation of one fact; (3) watermark — retention records 'every intent older than position T is retired' and a straggler gets a typed intent-retired refusal; bounded constant state, same idea as a GC threshold, but intent ids need an orderable component (today a hash of job and node) and the caller must handle the refusal; (4) parent-owned lifetime — a row is retired only when its originator (schema job, REPLACE chain, planner decision) is itself terminal and retired, so no retrier exists; needs every operation to name its originator and parent tables retained first; (5) fresh execution — rejected: breaks exactly-once, can resurrect a terminally failed operation. Integration owner's recommendation: (4) as the rule with (3) as the backstop for stragglers, (1) approximated by the unreferenced check, (2) only as a transition. No ruling yet; this quest must not seal before it.

Owner ruling 2026-11-11 (verbatim: 'i agree with 4+3 for the retention question'), answering the open retry-after-retirement question. RULE (alternative 4, parent-owned lifetime): a terminal replica_operations row is retired only when its originator (schema job, REPLACE chain, planner decision) is itself terminal and retired, so no live retrier can reach a retired row. BACKSTOP (alternative 3, watermark): retention records a retired-below position; any straggler retry of an intent below it receives a typed 'intent retired' refusal and never a fresh execution. Fresh execution of a retired intent (alternative 5) is ruled out. Consequences owed by this quest: every operation records its originator (planner-created ones do not today); intent ids gain an orderable component (the creation timestamp the row already carries is the candidate); schema jobs need their own terminal-and-retired rule first, as the longest-lived parents; callers handle the typed refusal (a schema job ends failed). Constraint retry-answer-needs-a-ruling is satisfied by this entry. Still unruled: statement-outcome dedupe horizon; inert tables.
